title: Advancing Fruit Quality Monitoring with Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Non-Destructive Technologies
abstract: Monitoring fruit quality is vital in modern agriculture and postharvest systems due to its impact on food security, economic sustainability, and consumer health. Traditional destructive sampling and manual inspection are time-consuming and inefficient. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with non-destructive sensing technologies offers a rapid, high-throughput alternative for quality assessment. This review explores the application of AI across pre- and postharvest stages using spectroscopic (e.g., NIR, THz), imaging (e.g., hyperspectral, X-ray), and sensor-based systems (e.g., electronic nose). It evaluates traditional machine learning (e.g., SVM, RF), deep learning (e.g., CNNs, GANs), and hybrid models, with a focus on real-time deployment, edge AI, and multimodal data fusion. AI-driven methods have achieved over 95% accuracy in tasks like ripeness classification and bruise detection, reducing postharvest losses by 20–40%. However, challenges remain, such as high sensor costs, model fragility under field conditions, and a lack of standardization. Future directions highlight explainable AI, IoT-enabled digital twins, and autonomous agri-robotics. Overall, this review underscores AI’s transformative potential in fruit quality monitoring, contingent on interdisciplinary collaboration and scalable implementation.

title: Advances and Emerging Trends in Monitoring and Predictive Technologies for Yoghurt Fermentation
abstract: Yoghurt fermentation is a dynamic and multiscale process in which microbial activity, mineral equilibrium, and protein reorganization collectively govern acidification kinetics, gel formation, texture, and product consistency. Conventional monitoring approaches, predominantly based on intermittent pH or titratable acidity measurements, provide limited insight into early biochemical, ionic, and microstructural transitions that critically influence fermentation outcomes. In response to these limitations, a wide range of advanced, non-destructive, and real-time monitoring techniques has emerged in recent years. This review systematically consolidates and evaluates developments across acoustic and mechanical sensing, optical spectroscopy and imaging, electrochemical and dielectric methods, molecular tools, and artificial intelligence–enabled hybrid systems for yoghurt fermentation monitoring and prediction. The comparative analysis links each technique to the specific physicochemical or biological phenomena it interrogates, while assessing practical considerations such as invasiveness, cost, data complexity, and industrial readiness. The review highlights how different methods complement one another in capturing acidification dynamics, casein micelle destabilization, gelation, and microbial performance, and emphasizes the growing role of data fusion and machine learning in enabling predictive and automated process control. By integrating dispersed advances into a single framework, this work addresses the lack of a unified perspective on yoghurt fermentation monitoring and provides a structured foundation for selecting, combining, and deploying sensing technologies in research, pilot, and industrial dairy processing environments. Overall, this review serves as a practical reference to rationally select and integrate advanced sensing and data-driven tools for yoghurt fermentation across laboratory and industrial scales.

title: Advances in Microwave-assisted Extraction Modeling: Mechanistic, Computational, and Data-driven Approaches
abstract: Microwave-assisted extraction (MAE) has emerged as an efficient and sustainable technology for recovering bioactive compounds from plant materials, food-processing residues, and agro-industrial by-products. However, the complex interactions among electromagnetic energy absorption, heat transfer, mass transfer, solvent characteristics, and plant-matrix properties create significant challenges for process understanding, optimization, and industrial scale-up. This review critically examines recent advances in MAE modeling, covering the progression from empirical and kinetic models to mechanistic, computational, and data-driven approaches. Fundamental aspects of microwave heating and transport phenomena are discussed, along with physics-based models describing electromagnetic, thermal, and mass-transfer processes. Advances in numerical and multiphysics simulations, including finite element, finite difference, and computational fluid dynamics approaches, are evaluated with emphasis on process visualization, optimization, and scale-up. The increasing role of machine-learning techniques, hybrid modeling strategies, physics-informed artificial intelligence, and digital twins in developing intelligent extraction systems is also highlighted. The strengths, limitations, applicability, and future potential of different modeling approaches are critically compared. The review demonstrates that integration of mechanistic knowledge with computational simulations and artificial intelligence can enhance predictive capability, improve process control, and accelerate the development of sustainable, scalable, and digitally enabled MAE technologies. title: Exploring Trends and Future Developments in the Application of Artificial Intelligence in Food Processing and Preservation
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming food processing and preservation, offering significant opportunities to improve efficiency, safety, quality, and sustainability. This systematic review examines the application of AI technologies in this field, with particular emphasis on machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and robotics. Using a PRISMA-based approach, literature published between 2015 and 2025 was analysed to identify major research trends, leading contributors, and emerging thematic areas. The review shows that AI has been widely applied in quality control and inspection, process optimisation, shelf-life prediction, intelligent packaging, predictive maintenance, and cold-chain monitoring. AI-driven systems have demonstrated strong capability in analysing complex datasets, detecting abnormalities, modelling food processes, improving decision-making, and enhancing food safety across the value chain. Bibliometric and thematic evidence further indicates that the field is rapidly expanding and increasingly interdisciplinary. However, most reported applications remain at laboratory or pilot scale, with limited industrial-scale implementation. Key barriers include data quality, model robustness, real-time integration, and limited cross-process deployment. Ultimately, these challenges underscore the need for ongoing research and development in AI technologies to realise their promise within the food business further. Future research directions encompass the amalgamation of AI with biotechnology, advancing more resilient and interpretable AI models, and formulating ethical standards for the appropriate application of AI in food processing and preservation. Therefore, this article serves as a significant resource for scholars, practitioners, and industry experts seeking to leverage the full capabilities of AI to elevate the food processing and preservation industry.

title: Optimization Strategies for Hybrid Drying Systems: Enhancing Energy Efficiency, Cost, and Quality in Food Processing
abstract: Abstract The increasing global demand for sustainable food processing practices, coupled with the need to address global energy issues and environmental pollution, has underscored the importance of optimizing drying technologies. While conventional drying methods, such as hot air drying, remain prevalent, they are highly energy-intensive and often compromise product quality. In response, hybrid drying systems (HDS), particularly those combining microwave, heat pump, or dehumidifier and renewable energy sources, have emerged as promising alternatives. However, their broader adoption is constrained by complex interactions between multiple heat and mass transfer mechanisms, which complicate process control, limit scalability, and hinder systematic optimization. This review critically evaluates existing optimization strategies for HDS, highlighting key limitations in current approaches that rely heavily on empirical, univariate, or fragmented methodologies. Relevant studies were identified through a structured literature search using the Scopus database, limited to articles published between 2020 and 2025. The review explores a spectrum of optimization tools, including statistical methods, AI-driven approaches, nature-inspired algorithms, and physics-based models, assessing their applicability, scalability, and integration potential. Emphasis is placed on aligning optimization strategies with specific decision-making parameters such as drying efficiency, energy use, cost, and product quality. The review further proposes a structured framework for selecting hybrid dryer configurations and optimization techniques based on defined objectives. By addressing current research gaps, this work provides insights that support the development of clean, efficient, and resilient food drying systems, with potential relevance to broader sustainability objectives, including the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: Automation and Robotics in the Food Industry: Cyber-Physical Systems, Digital Twins, and AI-Driven Quality Control in the Era of Industry 5.0
abstract: The food industry is experiencing a profound technological transformation fueled by the convergence of automation, robotics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) within the framework of Industry 5.0. At the core of this evolution are cyber-physical systems (CPS) and digital twins (DT), which enable real-time monitoring, adaptive control, and predictive analytics across food processing, packaging, and distribution. CPS brings together smart sensors, edge devices, and robotic platforms to form interconnected ecosystems that not only drive operational efficiency but also strengthen traceability, safety, and sustainability. Complementing this, digital twins serve as dynamic virtual counterparts of physical assets, enabling simulation-based decision-making, risk evaluation, and life-cycle optimization, all of which support proactive quality management. The integration of AI-driven algorithms enhances these architectures with advanced defect detection, predictive maintenance, and intelligent quality control, ensuring adherence to stringent food safety standards while simultaneously minimizing waste and conserving resources. Industry 5.0 goes a step further by embedding a human-centered perspective, where collaborative robots (cobots) and augmented intelligence systems assist workers in fostering resilience, adaptability, and mass customization. This holistic integration places food manufacturing at the intersection of smart production and societal well-being, establishing systems that are not only efficient but also ethically aligned with consumer expectations for transparency and sustainability. By examining the synergies of CPS, DT, and AI within the Industry 5.0 paradigm, this review highlights the technological trajectories and challenges in developing future-ready, intelligent, and human-centric food systems. title: Application of Artificial Intelligence–Based Methods for Foam Monitoring and Control in Fermentative Bioprocesses
abstract: Foam formation remains a major operational challenge in fermentative bioprocesses, affecting process stability, product quality, and industrial scalability. In the last decade, artificial intelligence (AI)–based approaches, including computer vision (CV), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL), have been increasingly applied for automated foam monitoring and control. This systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines to critically evaluate AI-driven methods for foam detection, quantification, and control in fermentation systems. Systematic searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore identified 566 records published between 2015 and 2025, of which 167 studies met the inclusion criteria and 89 were eligible for quantitative synthesis. Random-effects meta-analysis demonstrated that deep learning–based models significantly outperformed classical image processing approaches for foam-related tasks, with pooled coefficients of determination reaching R² = 0.88 (95% CI: 0.84–0.92) for foam height or volume prediction. Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies (I² = 72%), reflecting variability in experimental scale, datasets, and validation protocols. Risk of bias assessment using QUADAS-AI and PROBAST-AI revealed moderate methodological concerns in model validation and dataset representativeness, while overall certainty of evidence was rated as low to very low according to GRADE criteria, reflecting methodological limitations in model validation and dataset heterogeneity. These findings indicate that AI-based foam monitoring enables accurate, non-invasive, and real-time assessment in fermentative bioprocesses, but also highlight the need for standardized datasets, transparent validation strategies, and tighter integration with process control frameworks to support reliable industrial deployment.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Food Texture, Rheology and Sensory Attributes: Current Applications and Future Directions
abstract: Texture, rheological behaviour, and sensory perception are critical determinants of food quality, consumer acceptance, and processing performance. Conventional evaluation methods, including instrumental analyses and trained sensory panels, are labour-intensive, time-consuming, and often lack inter-laboratory reproducibility, limiting their application in rapid and scalable food quality assessment. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed this field by enabling accurate, data-driven prediction of complex physicochemical and sensory attributes from heterogeneous datasets. This review critically examines AI-driven approaches for predicting food texture, rheology, and sensory characteristics, covering classical machine learning, deep learning, graph neural networks, transfer learning, foundation models, and explainable AI. Across the studies synthesised in this review, classical machine learning and gradient-boosting models achieved coefficients of determination of R² = 0.94–0.98 for rheological and compositional prediction tasks, convolutional and transformer-based deep learning architectures reached correlations of r = 0.91–0.97 for texture attributes derived from imaging data, and electronic sensing and multimodal fusion approaches achieved classification accuracies of 91–99% while reducing false alarms by up to 31% relative to single-modality models. Particular emphasis is placed on integrating advanced sensing technologies, including hyperspectral imaging, near-infrared spectroscopy, computer vision, and electronic nose and tongue systems, with multimodal data fusion for comprehensive food quality evaluation. Applications across bakery, dairy, meat, plant-based products, emulsions, gels, and 3D-printed foods are discussed to highlight technological advances and industrial relevance. AI models consistently outperform conventional statistical methods by capturing complex nonlinear relationships among formulation, processing, structural, and sensory variables, thereby improving predictive accuracy, robustness, and scalability. Furthermore, explainable AI frameworks, including SHAP, LIME, and Grad-CAM, together with emerging generative AI and digital twin technologies, are enhancing model transparency and enabling predictive formulation and intelligent food design. However, most reviewed studies report internal cross-validation only, with few employing external, independent validation sets, and typical published datasets remain small (often fewer than 500 samples), which constrains generalisability across food categories. Despite challenges related to data standardisation, model generalizability, and regulatory implementation, continued advances in explainable and multimodal AI are expected to accelerate transparent, reliable, and scalable food quality assessment and product innovation.
